title: Help me! Could this work? (I'm new)

posts.author: Reiken
posts.body:
Hello,
I have zero experience with RPG makers so I wanted to know if my idea is actually possible to make.
My idea is to make essentially a dungeon crawler inspired by solo leveling and persona 5. The idea is the players real word effects the game (kinda like a habit tracker). E.G. Working out would actually increase the players character in game. There would also be some other things I want to add e.g. player fails to complete the daily tasks for that day then monsters will spawn in. I would also want things such as player making their own quest possible and maybe even a streak system. Could this all work and does a newbie like me stand a chance in making it? Also would it be too much to ask for me to try and make the dungeon completely randomised?
Thank you for reading

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
Randomize dungeons is tough, as it's not originally intended in RPG Maker. But there are plugins for it.
If you take one step back, you could also set up several dungeon layouts and pick one at random whenever the player enters a new stage. Also place items at random, etc. That's what I do in my game.
The other stuff is kind of vague. Like a "streak system". Of course, you can add a feature and call it that. But does it do, what you think of?
But I don't see any issue in your feature set. All is doable. You'll need to design them thoroughly, as they these features depend on eachother.
For a start, you should just jump in and check out what the RPG Maker can do. Learn about all the commands, check out the tutorials, etc. Step it up from there.

posts.author: Zia_
posts.body:
I chose MZ, as it's the newest, getting updates and I like the mapping more than in MV.
For a while, MV was preferred, as there are more custom Plugins available, but MZ is catching up, and there's almost everything ported or redone by now.
Today, I don't see a real reason not to take the newest, as you start over anyway.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Reiken said:
Which RPG maker should I be using?
Click to expand...
As said above, MZ has the most options added, including several things that do not exist in any other maker (like particle animations in addition to picture animations)
However, there is one disadvantage to MZ:
In MZ, a lot of the plugins have become obfuscated, and that makes compatibility patches almost impossible.
Which means that getting some of the more exotic plugins to work together very problematic.
it is unlikely that this would cause problems for a new user, but it should be mentioned.

posts.author: Robro33
posts.body:
Zia_ said:
For a while, MV was preferred, as there are more custom Plugins available, but MZ is catching up, and there's almost everything ported or redone by now.
Click to expand...
that being said, MV is much cheaper when it goes on sale, there still are plugin systems available on MV that arent present in MZ, and the largest suite of plugins made for it with active developers (Visustella) has obfuscated code. its much more difficult to get support and patches them than the Yanfly set for MV.
the MZ editor is more "feature complete" as it has features that in MV had to be added via plugins baked directly into it. It has many QoL changes in many areas over MV like mapping. its easy to transfer a map to an mz project when setting it up and then move it back to MV for use, but that requires owning both.

Well, sort of....I think the meaning may have gotten lost in interpretation, but I presume this:
Reiken said:
players real word effects the game [...] E.G. Working out would actually increase the players character in game.
Click to expand...
means he wants the real
world
to affect the game. Which means the player would need a device & companion app to be able to communicate with the game, likely via a server.
First of all, the companion app is entirely on your own. That's well outside the scope of RPG Maker.
Second, there isn't really networking support for RM either, and generally it's something you'd want to handle yourself for security reasons anyways.

Yea that's more for what I was going for.
Click to expand...
It'd definitely likely be more trouble than it's worth to implement. It's not impossible since the engine is open. But practically speaking, it's not really something feasible.
Depending on how jank or creative you want to be, you could just ask your players about their day.
If they lie, they are only cheating themselvess, right?
You could also just mask it; don't tell the players directly why the game is asking certain questions, which reduces the chances of the player trying to game it.
I can imagine having a gym in your game and the NPC can ask the player
"Did you work out recently?"
You'd need to make sure to use some language that indicates the NPC is asking about the player's real life.
Is not a great solution, but definitely a much smaller scope solution. And a bit janky too, but welcome to RM, home of the jank.
